analysis.title: US midterms: Blue wave ushers in gridlock
key_insights: Democrats are projected to retake both the House and Senate per AP and the major TV networks, ending unified Republican control of Washington. The scale of the win exceeded what markets had priced.
Nasdaq futures were down about 0.8%, S&P 500 futures about 0.6% and the Nikkei about 3% as the report was published. UBS says already fragile tech sentiment is likely amplifying the move.

UBS reads the result as a referendum on the administration, consistent with negative presidential approval and elevated oil prices, and cautions against reading it as a broad Democratic policy mandate.

UBS expects legislative friction rather than a policy reversal. Trump keeps veto power, Senate rules and divided government constrain large tax or spending bills, and the executive keeps broad authority over tariffs and foreign policy.

Democrats gain oversight powers, confirmation authority and more influence over spending and debt-limit talks. They also get a platform to test proposals on Social Security, healthcare and AI regulation ahead of 2028.
Trump said after the results that he will work with Democrats and does not want to veto everything.

UBS calls the 2027 debt-ceiling negotiations the clearest risk for bonds. Scheduled social-program cuts could be softened and defense spending raised, which could reverse an expected narrowing in deficits and increase Treasury supply.
UBS still expects inflation to moderate, the Fed to finish raising rates and Treasury yields to settle lower.

Greater congressional oversight need not derail the AI investment cycle. State and local rules matter more for data-center timing and location, and the Texas result may matter more for individual projects than the change in Congress.
UBS raised its aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027, while global investors weigh overinvestment, financing and monetization risks more heavily.

Positioning guidance: UBS sees possible near-term volatility in tech and regulation-sensitive sectors but no case for an immediate strategic shift. It favors reducing single-name concentration, rebalancing oversized tech exposure and tilting toward quality AI value-chain companies.
UBS sees attractive income in high-quality short- to medium-term bonds and is cautious on the longest maturities because of persistent deficits and heavy issuance.

Swiss CPI rose 1.5% y/y in October, from 1.0% in September and the highest in almost three years, driven by heating oil, petrol and diesel and a weaker franc. Core inflation was 0.5%. Headline is above the SNB's 1.2% Q4 forecast.
UBS expects the SNB to hike twice in H1 2027 to 0.5%. A December hike depends on confirmation of economic progress. UBS expects the franc to gain against the euro and the dollar over 12 months.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term volatility is likely from politics and regulatory scrutiny. UBS advises rebalancing oversized tech exposure and tilting toward quality AI value-chain companies, not abandoning positions.
Demand remains strong and UBS raised its AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027. Volatility may favor financially strong platforms and infrastructure providers.

earnings_insights: UBS says strong earnings support its constructive view on equities. The report gives no company-level figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest in almost three years and above the SNB's 1.2% Q4 forecast, but within the 0-2% range. Energy-driven, so UBS sees no urgent SNB response.
Core remains contained, which points to a slower SNB response.
October headline CPI came in above this.
Stabilizing energy prices offset stronger second-round effects.
Two hikes expected in the first half of 2027, normalizing policy.

trade_ideas.description: Reduce single-name concentration and rebalance oversized technology exposure toward quality AI value-chain companies
trade_ideas.rationale: Politically driven weakness can be used to rebalance or build exposure gradually.
trade_ideas.risk: Near-term volatility in tech and regulation-sensitive areas.

trade_ideas.description: Own high-quality short- to medium-term bonds for income and diversification, cautious on the longest maturities
trade_ideas.rationale: Current yields offer attractive income, while persistent deficits and heavy issuance argue for caution on long maturities.
trade_ideas.risk: Debt-ceiling brinkmanship and larger Treasury supply.

risk_factors: 2027 debt-ceiling negotiations could soften scheduled social-program cuts and raise defense spending, reversing an expected narrowing in deficits and raising Treasury supply.
Political brinkmanship could raise bond-market volatility.
Investor concern about AI overinvestment, financing and monetization.
Possible markets pricing of 2028 outcomes, which UBS calls premature.
State-level rules, including the Texas result, may affect data-center timing and location.
Swiss energy-led inflation above the SNB forecast.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq futures were down about 0.8% and S&P 500 futures about 0.6% after the results, and the Nikkei fell about 3%.
UBS expects higher volatility could become the new normal for AI-related equities.
Possible 2027 debt-ceiling brinkmanship could raise bond-market volatility.
geopolitical: US midterm elections: Democrats projected to win the House and Senate, ending unified Republican control.
Trump retains broad executive authority over tariffs and foreign policy.
Elevated oil prices cited as a factor in the election backdrop.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says the result does not change the medium-term fundamental outlook. Strong earnings support the constructive equity view, and politically driven weakness can be used to build exposure gradually.
tension_points.bear_case: The Democratic win was larger than priced. Futures fell, tech sentiment was already fragile, and debt-ceiling talks in 2027 could raise Treasury supply and bond volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A material policy change that alters the fundamental outlook. UBS says it would adjust portfolios only in that case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Divided government and the presidential veto should constrain sweeping legislation, producing friction rather than a policy reversal.
theme_stances.evidence: Expect sand in the legislative gears, not sharp policy changes.

theme_stances.key_argument: Federal oversight is unlikely to derail AI investment, and underlying demand remains strong.
2027 debt-ceiling talks could widen deficits and increase Treasury supply, raising bond volatility.
theme_stances.evidence: Debt talks remain the clearest risk for bonds.
